Replay

Claimball Parties and browser play

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Identity and admissionConnections and savesAcceptance and limitsReopening a saved Party

Set RCB_ROOM_SERVICE to a provisioned Replay Room service to expose Create party, Join party, Watch only, Copy invite and Rejoin recent. The same controls work in native Godot and the browser. Standalone native sessions remain available when no service is configured; Solo uses its local session.

Native configuration uses RCB_* environment variables. Browser configuration uses the lowercase suffix as a URL query: room_service, room_local, name, port, latency, and so on. This is the existing launch-parameter adapter. Browser profiles load before connection controls become available. Browser multiplayer uses the configured Party service and WebRTC transport.

Identity and admission#

Personal reconnect identity and display name use the replay-claimball profile namespace. Party credentials use replay-claimball-rooms, separately from that personal identity. Native Party records default to user://claimball_rooms.sqlite3 (RCB_ROOMS_DB overrides it). Browser identity, name and Party records use the existing IndexedDB adapters. Explicit test tokens, bots and RCB_PERSIST=0 retain their documented profile bypass behavior.

The creator invites up to three trusted peers. An invite explicitly permits friends to host and keep the match running. Watch only selects seat zero and disables checkpoint acceptance for that session. Observers cannot issue player actions; the fixture verifies their role before and after migration/rejoin. Invite admission and later credential-based rejoin remain distinct operations.

Connections and saves#

  • RCB_ROOM_LOCAL=1 enables the existing literal-loopback development exception. Production services use their normal secure URL and admission configuration.
  • RCB_ROOM_ADDRESS and RCB_PORT describe native gameplay reachability. The provisioned grant supplies the actual Room identity and connection information.
  • RCB_ROOM_CA can supply a native trusted certificate. RCB_ICE_JSON and RCB_ROOM_RELAY feed the existing RTC/relay credential adapters.
  • The first connected player starts the match. Handoff is available to an authority with an eligible successor. Claims/smoothing/effects reset at an epoch change; clients still predict one avatar plus the ball.
  • Save · F5 in a provisioned Party publishes through the service. The authority gets a publication receipt; later successful publication replaces that room's saved progress. RCB_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS optionally requests the supported cadence. Party publication does not create a browser-local game-save slot.
  • Standalone native file saves still use the matching host profile. Browser Solo uses named local checkpoint slots, described in the session guide.

The Room service supports operator-selected checkpoint model claimball with content C3 (0x52434c41494d4233). Requests cannot choose executable validation code. The backend validates and persists complete authority checkpoints, including the roster and ball/player state. No game schema changed for the Party integration.

Acceptance and limits#

Shell
REPLAY_CLAIMBALL_ONLINE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output nix develop --command bash tests/replay_claimball_online/run.sh

Local native Party UI, four-browser planned handoff and owner-SIGKILL paths are covered. The browser fixture checks real RTC traffic, complete moving checkpoint restore, new spikes, retained/new chat, observer rejoin, fresh host return with retained personal profile/invite, one-avatar prediction, common authoritative worlds, and service publication before/after migration. An independent reader validates the persisted C3 checkpoints.

An initial browser run ended with Fenced before handoff. The diagnostic planned and crash runs pass, but the original cause remains unestablished; this is retained as an open issue. No clock, lease, fault or recovery limit was relaxed. See the full receipts. Native WSS and browser whole-party restoration have separate acceptance receipts. Public deployment, broader network/OS/hardware testing, consecutive failures, Steam and human parity remain further work. RCB_PROBE=1 enables extra local checkpoint diagnostics and is used by the browser fixture.

Reopening a saved Party#

After all game processes have stopped, Rejoin recent can restore the service's published checkpoint through the existing explicit restore grant. The service must retain its database and checkpoint, and the returning trusted host must retain its credentials. The new authority epoch preserves the published world; later progress can be rolled back. The UI reports that restoration. An observer can re-register first but cannot start an authority runtime. Other players rejoin their prior seats.

Both the native trusted-WSS and browser RTC fixtures kill/restart the service as well as all game processes. They validate the saved frame before shutdown and the continued publication afterward. A common world check covers post-restore play. This is recovery of explicitly published progress, not a promise to retain every last live tick or cosmetic chat line after total process loss.

The recovery notice uses the shared backup-status observation. It distinguishes an approved backup from preparation, stale progress or uncertain control; a prior host change does not imply the next backup is ready.
